purpose: Backend runtime manifest for the Component 1 pipelines retrained in October 2026 on the condition-matched farmer dataset.

transformation.description: None. The pipelines were trained under the same library versions as this backend, so each runtime artifact is a byte-identical copy of the research export (runtime_sha256 equals original_artifact.sha256).

models.name: drc_prediction
models.test_metrics: R2 0.770, MAE 0.84 pp; within +/-1 pp 61.5%, +/-2 pp 95.9% (122 held-out rows)
models.deployment_note: Copy of the CV-selected, train-fitted pipeline. Not refit on the full dataset. visible_latex_condition drives almost all of the prediction; when it is missing the pipeline fills the most common training value (Normal). month and day_of_year are derived by the backend from the observation-local timestamp.
models.dataset_provenance: condition-matched farmer records (5 estates, Jun-Sep 2026) with Open-Meteo weather; DRC values normalized by the dataset author, not original field measurements
models.target_warning: DRC values in the training data were normalized to Kudaligama chart entries and aligned with the visible latex condition by the dataset author.

models.name: price_estimation
models.test_metrics: R2 0.901, MAE 6.70 LKR/kg (about 2.3%); within +/-5 LKR 45.1%, +/-10 LKR 79.5%, +/-15 LKR 94.3% (122 held-out rows, scored from estimated DRC)
models.deployment_note: Copy of the CV-selected, train-fitted pipeline. Not refit on the full dataset. The target is the price per kg of field latex, defined as farm-gate latex price (Rs per kg dry rubber) x DRC / 100, so watery (low-DRC) latex is worth less. The latex_drc_pct input was trained on the estimated DRC (as the app supplies it from drc_prediction), so the score includes DRC estimation error.
models.dataset_provenance: price derived from farm-gate latex levels (Rubber Development Department; Jun-Sep 2026 levels estimated from Central Bank of Sri Lanka FOB prices) x DRC
models.target_warning: Training prices were derived by formula from farm-gate levels and DRC; June-September 2026 farm-gate levels are estimates, not published prices.

models.name: tapping_advisory
models.test_metrics: accuracy 0.934, macro-F1 0.925; recall High 1.00, Moderate 1.00, Low 0.76 (122 held-out rows)
models.deployment_note: Copy of the CV-selected, train-fitted classifier bundle ({'pipeline', 'label_encoder', 'classes', 'warning'}). Not refit on the full dataset. predict_proba column order is exactly the classes order above (High=0, Low=1, Moderate=2).
models.dataset_provenance: condition-matched farmer records (5 estates, Jun-Sep 2026) with Open-Meteo weather; next-6 h rain input is the Open-Meteo forecast issued a day earlier
models.target_warning: Rule-derived proxy labels from rainfall thresholds, judged on rain that actually fell; the model sees only the forecast issued beforehand (no added noise). NOT expert-verified tapping advice.

research_provenance.source_dataset: ml-research/component_1_weather_tapping/data/raw/Combined_Rubber_Latex_Dataset_Condition_Matched.xlsx (610 farmer records used; prepared by src/00_prepare_realistic_dataset.py)
research_provenance.embedded_preprocessing: Median imputation (numeric; StandardScaler for the tapping model) and most-frequent imputation + one-hot encoding (categorical, handle_unknown='ignore') are embedded inside each sklearn Pipeline and were fitted on the training partition only.

known_limitations: Trained on 610 farmer records from 5 estates over June-September 2026; results may not hold for other estates or seasons.
DRC values were normalized and aligned with the visible latex condition by the dataset author, so the DRC model mainly reflects that condition; weather alone barely changes it.

Price is a formula of farm-gate level and DRC, and tapping labels come from a rainfall rule. Their scores are realistic because the models were trained on what the app has (estimated DRC, an issued forecast), not because they learned verified market or agronomic behaviour.
forecast_rain_next_6h_mm in training is the Open-Meteo forecast issued about a day earlier; at runtime the weather provider supplies a current forecast, which is usually a little more accurate.
Models were fitted on the training partition only (never refit on the full dataset).
month and day_of_year are derived from observation-local timestamps; any timezone conversion is explicit (never silent UTC).

Out-of-range and missing values are treated as missing and imputed inside the pipeline (median for numbers, most common value for categories); the pipelines reject non-finite (inf) inputs, so callers validate first.
Estates not seen in training (anything other than Estate 01-05) are ignored by the one-hot encoder; estate_name is never a model feature.
